label: NAP 8-port
notes: The box a technician opens at the pole: 8 drop ports, the feeder entry that feeds them, and two 12-fibre trays. `ports` counts CABLES, not drop adapters - docs/PARTS.md says so and engine/network.js compares the spans touching a node against it - and the two counts differ by exactly the entry the feeder arrives through: CommScope's SSC2811-SM-8 end box publishes 'Distribution capacity 1(Input) + 8(Drop)', one inlet adapter (red) and eight outlet adapters (black), and Prysmian's MTWB lists 16 drop ports against 'No. of Input cable ports 1 top and 1 bottom'. This row said 8 until 2026-11-27, which made a NAP loaded with the eight drops it is sold for plus the feeder reaching it read '9 cables into 8 ports' - the box the design had just bought, reported as the wrong box, on the one plant it exists for. 9 is the END box, not the cascade variant: the SSC2811-SM-9U SubBox publishes 1(Input) + 1(Extension) + 8(Drop) = 10, so a daisy-chained NAP belongs in a box with a cascade port - nap-16 carries the extra entry and the auto-designer already assigns it from 9 cables upward. Drop count, trays and the 12-fibre trays are typical of the class, not one datasheet: IEC 61753-1 covers the closure's qualification and publishes no capacity figure. Replace with the bought closure's datasheet before ordering.
